novelty.justification: The claim predicts that molecular-model SAEs will recover "monosemantic features corresponding to chemically meaningful functional groups" that are "causally editable," so its novelty route is chiefly transferring an established SAE concept-discovery and steering paradigm to SMILES and molecular-graph models. Searches using "sparse autoencoder molecular transformer functional groups," "SAE ChemBERTa MolFormer interpretability," and "dictionary learning SMILES activation steering" identify the closest conceptual precedent as InterPLM-style SAE discovery and steering of biological concepts in protein language models, while chemistry-specific work such as the 2023 Substructure Mask Explanation paper and FARM (2024) already studies chemically meaningful substructure representations without SAEs. Moving from those precedents to SMARTS-aligned functional-group features is a direct domain transfer with useful chemistry-specific operationalization, but neither SAE monosemanticity nor feature steering supplies a new core relationship beyond the established template.
